hints.title: Degree Balance Invariant Obstacle
hints.text: The town judge trusts nobody and is trusted by all other n - 1 people in town. How can tracking net directed trust degrees identify the unique judge candidate in a single pass?

hints.title: Net In-Degree Equation Invariant
hints.text: For person i: each trust edge (a, i) increments i trust score by 1; each trust edge (i, b) decrements i trust score by 1. The judge must have net trust score equal to n - 1.

hints.title: Single Degree Array Procedure
hints.text: Allocate an integer array trust_score of length n + 1. For each pair (a, b) in trust: decrement trust_score[a] and increment trust_score[b]. Iterate person i from 1 to n: if trust_score[i] == n - 1, return i. Return -1 if no candidate satisfies the condition.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single pass over trust relationships followed by a linear scan over N people.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Building two separate full adjacency matrices takes O(N^2) space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single 1D degree array of size N + 1 uses minimal O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combining in-degree and out-degree into a single balance metric in_deg - out_deg == n - 1.
